title: Bathymetric Reconstruction Using Time-Series Satellite Images and Minimal In Situ Data
content: This study proposes a method for reconstructing bathymetric terrain heights using time-series satellite images combined with a bathymetric interpolation technique. Conventional approaches of bathymetric surveys require LiDAR or echo sounders, which require significant cost and time. To overcome this limitation, we propose an algorithm to reconstruct an internal digital elevation model (DEM) of terrains under water bodies. We extract water boundaries from time-series satellite images. The extracted boundaries are treated as contour lines of bathymetric terrain, whose elevation values are not known. The contour lines are used as constraints during a hydrological bathymetric interpolation process. By assigning a true elevation to one water boundary and utilizing elevation values of nearby terrain, we reconstruct a bathymetric DEM. We can estimate a new water level from a new satellite image by overlaying a new water boundary on the bathymetric DEM reconstructed. We can validate the bathymetric DEM by comparing the estimated water level with the reference in situ water level. The proposed method was tested on three reservoirs using high-resolution KOMPSAT-3A images. With one reference water boundary and five nonreference water boundaries, the proposed method achieved an overall mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.61 m using six validation images for each reservoir, with MAEs of 0.61, 0.75, and 0.47 m for Nogok, Maegok, and Pungdo, respectively. These results show that time-series water boundaries can serve as effective constraints for bathymetric reconstruction and water-level estimation in small- and medium-sized reservoirs with limited in situ measurements.
author: Hongjun Youn, Taejung Kim

title: Maize Plant Height Estimation Using UAV and PlanetScope Imagery: A Comparison of 3-D Point Cloud and Machine Learning Approaches
content: Plant height (PH) is an essential indicator of crop growth and development, playing a critical role in field management and yield estimation. While recent advancements in remote sensing technologies have improved PH measurement capabilities, existing methods often encounter challenges related to accuracy, spatial resolution, and environmental conditions. In this study, we utilized low-altitude uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery and Planet satellite remote sensing data to explore PH measurement methods based on 3-D reconstructed point clouds and inversion from spectral and texture features. First, a 3-D point cloud method was used to generate a canopy height model (CHM) from a digital surface model (DSM) and a digital terrain model (DTM). Second, this study compared the accuracy of four machine learning methods: eXtreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest (RF), partial least-squares regression (PLSR), and support vector regression (SVR), for PH inversion at the field scale. The results show that the direct 3-D point cloud method is the most accurate for PH estimation, achieving an  $R^{2}$  of 0.98. For the machine learning inversion, the fusion of texture and spectral features consistently yielded the best performance for both data sources. Using high-resolution UAV imagery, XGBoost and RF models achieved the highest performance with an  $R^{2}$  of 0.74. With 3-m PlanetScope imagery, the XGBoost model was the top performer, reaching a maximum  $R^{2}$  of 0.59. On the contrary, the SVR model was consistently outperformed across all scenarios, highlighting the importance of appropriate model selection. Ultimately, high-resolution UAV imagery provided more accurate and reliable data for PH inversion compared to PlanetScope imagery. This study confirms the superiority of direct 3-D measurement and provides a clear guide for feature engineering and model selection in spectral-based PH estimation, providing new directions for future crop monitoring and precision agriculture research.
author: Ke Li, Qing Li, Yanan Wei, Dalei Hao, Weijian Yu, Yelu Zeng

title: From Relation to Structure: Spatial-Semantic Guidance and Structure Refinement Network for Multimodal Remote Sensing Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation is a fundamental task in remote sensing image (RSI) interpretation, aiming at pixel-wise classification of land cover. Recently, multimodal RSI semantic segmentation has attracted significant attention for its ability to alleviate the information bottleneck inherent in unimodal methods. However, existing multimodal methods often emphasize feature alignment and complementarity while overlooking the inherent coexistence and mutually exclusive relationships among land covers, frequently resulting in fragmented predictions. Moreover, achieving fine-grained boundary segmentation remains a crucial challenge. To address these challenges, we propose R2SNet, a spatial-semantic guidance and structure refinement network for multimodal RSI segmentation. The core innovation of R2SNet lies in a progressive optimization strategy that guides from semantic relations modeling to spatial structure refinement via three collaborative modules. Specifically, the asymmetric dual-branch (ADB) encoder performs modality-specific extraction of semantic and geometric features to mitigate computational redundancy and modal interference. Subsequently, the spatial-semantic guided cross-modal fusion (SGCF) module explicitly embeds spatial-semantic priors into the fusion process to suppress unreasonable relationships. Finally, the progressive structure refinement (PSR) decoder aggregates multiscale contexts and employs an eight-directional selective scanning mechanism to enhance structural integrity and refine boundaries. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen, ISPRS Potsdam, DDHR, and WHU-OPT synthetic aperture radar (SAR) datasets demonstrate that R2SNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly regarding semantic consistency and boundary precision. The code will be available at: https://github.com/bnu-wgy/R2SNet
author: Guangyi Wei, Qianpeng Chong, Zhenxi Wang, Zongyao Yin, Dan Hu, Yinggang Zhang, Xianchuan Yu

title: Adaptive Chirplet Transform and Its Application in Sedimentary Cycle Division
content: Sedimentary cycle division serves as a core geological theory for analyzing depositional environments and holds significant guiding importance for reservoir distribution prediction. Time–frequency (TF) analysis is a key technique in this context, and its effectiveness depends on the ability to clearly reveal variations in tuning frequency caused by changes in formation thickness. To improve the energy concentration of TF representations (TFRs), this article proposes an adaptive chirplet transform (ACT) for more accurately characterizing sedimentary cycles. The method first locates the instantaneous frequency (IF) trajectory of each mode within the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain using a local maximum criterion. Subsequently, based on the located trajectories, an adaptive chirp-rate estimator (AC) is constructed to accurately capture the frequency-modulation characteristics of each mode. Then, an effective window is defined according to the TF spectral energy distribution theory to delineate the distribution area of TF energy for each mode. Finally, based on the AC, the chirplet transform is adaptively constructed within the effective window corresponding to each mode. The theoretical analysis and synthetic signal experiments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances the energy concentration of the TFR while maintaining excellent signal reconstruction fidelity. Furthermore, analysis results of ACT on three typical geological models of sedimentary cycles and field seismic data show that this method can effectively identify sedimentary cycle patterns, indicating promising application potential.
author: Peng Chen, Hui Chen, Huailiang Li, Ying Hu, Xuping Chen, Yutao Xie

title: MGSC-Net: Multisemantic Guided Spatial–Frequency Collaborative Network for UAV-Based Infrared and Visible Image Fusion
content: Infrared and visible image fusion (IVIF) plays a critical role in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based all-weather aerial perception. However, in aerial scenarios, thermal targets are typically small scaled and easily submerged in complex backgrounds. Existing methods often face a severe feature compromise dilemma: enhancing the saliency of tiny infrared targets tends to oversmooth the vast visible background textures, whereas improving background clarity inevitably attenuates the thermal energy. This phenomenon primarily stems from the incompatibility between isomorphic networks and dual-modal heterogeneous data, where fragile small target signals are easily diluted in the spatial domain. To fundamentally alleviate these issues and achieve a highly robust cross-modal feature expression, this article proposes a multisemantic guided spatial–frequency collaborative network (MGSC-Net). In particular, the network adopts an asymmetric architecture at the encoder, designing a dual-branch extraction mechanism to independently decouple the thermal features of small targets and high-fidelity visible textures. In the fusion stage, a spatial–frequency collaborative strategy is introduced, utilizing frequency-domain priors to accurately anchor tiny targets and adaptively guide the fusion of spatial semantics. In the decoding stage, a progressive cross-scale reconstruction framework and a composite loss function are formulated. Extensive experiments on UAV and common datasets demonstrate that the proposed MGSC-Net achieves superior performance in both subjective and objective evaluations. It establishes an excellent visual balance between tiny targets and complex backgrounds, effectively improving the detection accuracy of downstream UAV vision tasks. The GitHub link is https://github.com/nchuhxn/MGSC-Net
author: Xiaonan He, Yukun Xia, Jianyao Li, Congxuan Zhang, Zhen Chen

title: Knowledge-Infused Temporal Fusion Transformer for Interpretable Riverbank Deformation Forecasting Using Sentinel-1 InSAR Time Series
content: Forecasting riverbank deformation requires characterizing complex spatiotemporal heterogeneity governed by coupled hydro-meteorological forcing and site-specific geomorphology. Although deep learning has shown promise for geohazard prediction, existing models for fluvial instability largely operate as black boxes, lacking both physical transparency and spatial transferability. This study proposes the knowledge-infused variational mode decomposition (VMD)-temporal fusion Transformer (TFT), knowledge-infused VMD-TFT (KI-VTFT), a physically constrained and interpretable framework that embeds domain knowledge into data-driven forecasting through two complementary pathways: 1) signal-level priors, injected via Bayesian-optimized VMD (BO-VMD), which partitions displacement into trend, periodic, and residual components; and 2) spatial-level priors, encoded through seven static geomorphic attributes that condition predictions on terrain-controlled susceptibility. The framework was applied to continuous displacement fields derived from 177 Sentinel-1 images (2021–2024) using small baseline subset interferometric synthetic aperture radar (SBAS-InSAR) across three subreaches of the Lower Yangtze River (LYR). At the five-step (60-day) forecasting horizon, KI-VTFT achieved a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 2.29 mm and an R2 of 0.97, reducing RMSE by 25.96%–65.12% relative to gated recurrent units (GRUs), long short-term memory (LSTM), temporal convolutional networks (TCNs), and Transformer baselines. Interpretability analysis revealed that VMD components drove 64.52% of encoder feature importance, while distance to thalweg (22.51%) and elevation (20.78%) dominated the static controls; temporal attention weights peaked during the May–August flood season, consistent with regional hydrological cycles. Independent validation using uncrewed aerial vehicle and uncrewed surface vessel (UAV–USV) bathymetric surveys, acoustic Doppler current profiler (ADCP) flow measurements, and sediment sampling supported the physical plausibility of model-identified drivers. Furthermore, zero-shot transfer to the separate Wuwei Reach maintained an RMSE of 2.77 mm without retraining, outperforming the strongest baseline, the Transformer (3.65 mm), under identical conditions and demonstrating the framework’s potential for cross-reach generalization.
author: Weijie Ding, Heqin Cheng, Zhaocai Wang, Dongping Chen, Junhao Wu, Ruonan Bao, Wenqiu Qu, Irene Cheng

title: Efficient 3-D Imaging Algorithm for Multilayer Dielectrics Based on MIMO-SAR System
content: The millimeter-wave (MMW) multiple-input multiple-output synthetic aperture radar (MIMO-SAR) system is highly valued in nondestructive testing due to its high resolution, robust penetration, and multidimensional data acquisition. Nevertheless, most existing imaging techniques are constrained to free-space or half-space scenarios, which typically leads to spatial blurring and low computational efficiency in multilayered dielectric applications. This study addresses these challenges by proposing an accurate and computationally efficient imaging algorithm for multilayered targets. The algorithm is developed based on a scalar Green’s function formulation for multilayer dielectric media, incorporates transverse-wavenumber continuity conditions at the interfaces, and employs spherical wave decomposition for efficient wavefield expansion. By integrating the fast Fourier transform (FFT) with multilayer phase compensation, the method achieves accurate focusing while maintaining high computational efficiency. Simulation and experimental results confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves comparable imaging quality with significantly improved computational efficiency compared with conventional approaches.
author: Xu Chen, Changyu Liu, Yilin Jiang, Bin Deng, Mengxiao Hao, Yu Wang, Muran Guo

title: Model, Source, and Analysis of BiSAR Maritime Moving Target’s Spatial Resolution
content: High-resolution imaging of maritime moving targets is of critical importance for maritime domain awareness and defense applications. Bistatic synthetic aperture radar (BiSAR) enables imaging for both stationary scenes and dynamic targets, where spatial resolution serves as a fundamental metric for system design and performance evaluation. While the resolution for static scenes can be derived from platform kinematics, it is invalid for moving targets owing to unknown translational motion and 3-D oscillations. Two fundamental limitations hinder current resolution analysis for moving targets: 1) direct application of such static-scene formulations to moving targets yields inaccurate resolution results, leading to failure of the system design; and 2) the resolution of moving targets depends on numerous factors, necessitating both quantitative and qualitative understanding of its statistical behavior. To address this issue, the resolution model and the physical source of BiSAR maritime moving targets have been systematically established and comprehensively characterized. First, the echo signal model of a maritime moving target in BiSAR is established, and the 2-D spatial resolution model is derived based on the gradient resolution theory. Subsequently, the azimuth resolution contribution index (ARCI) is proposed to quantitatively evaluate the individual contributions of the transmitter, receiver, and target motion to the azimuth resolution. Finally, a comprehensive analysis was carried out to investigate the time-varying characteristics of resolution and ARCI, as well as to analyze the impact of sea states, target rotation parameters, and platform configuration. The validity of the proposed ARCI and the derived theoretical framework is confirmed through numerical simulations.
author: Junjie Wu, Qing Yang, Junyan Li, Zhongyu Li, Qian Liu, Jianyu Yang

title: CCEM-Net: Conflict-Aware Cross Evidential Modulation for Hyperspectral Change Detection
content: Hyperspectral change detection (HSCD) remains challenging due to spectral inconsistency across bitemporal observations, heterogeneous spatial change patterns, and ambiguous decision boundaries that induce predictive uncertainty. Existing methods mainly rely on deterministic representation learning, lacking mechanisms to model uncertainty and resolve such conflicts, often resulting in overconfident and unreliable predictions. To address these issues, we propose CCEM-Net, a conflict-aware evidential deep learning (EDL) framework for reliable HSCD. Specifically, a change-aware interaction (CAI) module is introduced to model cross-temporal dependencies, suppress pseudo-changes, and enhance change-relevant responses via dual gating. A parallel adaptive multiscale spectral and spatial (AMSS) module further captures heterogeneous patterns through temporal-difference-guided multiscale feature aggregation. To handle decision ambiguity, we develop a conflict-aware cross evidential modulation (CCEM) mechanism that models branch predictions as Dirichlet distributions to quantify uncertainty. By measuring interbranch conflict via Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence, CCEM adaptively modulates evidence strength. Subsequently, reliable decision-level fusion is performed using the Yager rule. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that CCEM-Net consistently achieves the superior performance in both accuracy and reliability compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods. The code will be publicly available at: https://github.com/fwx0314/CCEM-Net
author: Shufang Xu, Wenxuan Fei, Shuyu Fei, Runhua Sheng, Hongmin Gao

title: Sparse Tensor Attention for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a fundamental task for resolving the mixed pixel problem by decomposing a hyperspectral image (HSI) into constituent endmembers and their corresponding abundances. Although deep-learning-based HU methods have achieved promising performance, most rely on manually designed network architectures that encode spatial–spectral priors only implicitly, limiting their interpretability and ability to model complex spatial–spectral characteristics. To address this limitation, we propose a self-supervised sparse tensor attention (TA) framework for HU, termed STU. The proposed method builds upon the mathematical connection between self-attention and Tucker decomposition and exploits the nonlocal spatial–spectral self-similarity and low-rank structure inherent in HSIs. Specifically, pairwise dependencies among local spatial–spectral cubes are encoded into a sparse tensorized attention core, which is projected through mode-wise low-rank factor matrices to recover the abundance representations. The resulting abundances are constrained to satisfy the abundance nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints and are subsequently combined with a learnable endmember matrix under the linear mixture model (LMM) to reconstruct the observed HSI. This formulation integrates data-adaptive nonlocal dependency modeling, multilinear low-rank representation, and physically consistent endmember-abundance estimation within a unified framework. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that STU achieves competitive or superior performance compared with representative model-based and deep-learning methods.
author: Jingran Wang, Fengchao Xiong, Zhiyuan Wen, Zhuang Zhao, Jun Zhou, Yuntao Qian

title: Dual-Path Learning Toward Open-Vocabulary Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images
content: While the landscape of closed-set oriented object detection has been revolutionized in recent years, extending this success to the instances of unseen categories, the core challenge of open-vocabulary object detection (OVD), remains a formidable hurdle. Prevailing methods often resort to a dedicated student detector to channel the cross-modal knowledge from pretrained vision-language models (VLMs), thereby enabling open-vocabulary generalization. However, these approaches, which primarily manifest as either knowledge distillation or pseudo-labeling frameworks, suffer from a fundamental tradeoff: biased region proposal network (RPN) yields poor recall for target objects, while shared detection head induces catastrophic forgetting of base classes. To overcome these limitations, we propose DPNet, a dedicated end-to-end dual-path network for open-vocabulary oriented object detection in remote sensing scenarios. First, we introduce a parameter-efficient multiscale adapter (MSA) that activates hierarchical features from a frozen vision-language encoder, enabling a category-agnostic network to generate high-quality proposals for target objects with varying scales. Second, a decoupled detection pipeline is formulated for base and target classes. This divide-and-conquer fashion alleviates the inherent optimization conflict, preserving base-class recognition fidelity while effectively learning target concepts. By circumventing the need for a student detector, DPNet offers a more streamlined and efficient architecture. Extensive experiments on two standard remote sensing benchmarks—DIOR and DOTA—validate that our solution achieves competitive performance, significantly outperforming pioneering approaches in both base-class precision and novel-class discovery under zero-shot settings. The source code will be available at https://github.com/yanqingyao1994/DPNet
author: Yanqing Yao, Xiang Yuan, Gong Cheng

title: Spatial–Temporal–Spectral Unified Modeling for Remote Sensing Dense Prediction
content: Despite advances in deep learning for remote sensing dense prediction, a unified framework for handling heterogeneous data, multiple tasks, and diverse semantic category sets remains elusive. Concretely, multiple correlated dense prediction tasks (e.g., semantic segmentation and change detection) are often modeled independently, requiring separate networks or task-specific decoder heads. Moreover, the semantic label space is typically fixed during training, so changing the target class subset requires modifying and retraining the prediction head. Here, we introduce the spatial–temporal–spectral unified network (STSUN), a unified framework for remote sensing dense prediction. The model employs metadata-informed unified representations generated via hypernetworks, enabling adaptation to inputs with variable spatial resolutions, temporal lengths, and spectral band configurations. Furthermore, it unifies diverse dense prediction tasks within a single architecture through learnable task embeddings and semantic category embeddings that support multiple class subsets represented during training. Experiments under scenario-level joint training on datasets with diverse spatial–temporal–spectral configurations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for modeling multiple dense prediction tasks and semantic class subsets within a single model.
author: Sijie Zhao, Feng Liu, Xueliang Zhang, Hao Chen, Pengfeng Xiao, Junjue Wang, Weihao Xuan, Naoto Yokoya, Lei Bai

title: Beyond Text: Bridging Speech and Satellite Imagery for Efficient Visual Grounding
content: While remote sensing visual grounding (RSVG) has emerged as a crucial bridge for human–machine interaction in Earth observation, existing methods rely exclusively on textual queries. In time-critical applications such as disaster rescue and emergency response, this reliance restricts hands-free operation and strips away vital prosodic cues like tone and emphasis, which are highly effective for disambiguating complex geospatial targets. To overcome these limitations, we formally introduce the task of audio-driven RSVG (Audio-RSVG) and construct Audio-detectIon in optical remote sensing (DIOR), a large-scale dataset simulating real-world acoustic environments with diverse timbres and background noise conditions. Furthermore, we propose RSTalker, a robust end-to-end framework designed to directly align speech signals with aerial imagery. By bypassing cascaded automatic speech recognition (ASR) pipelines, RSTalker prevents transcription error propagation, particularly regarding remote sensing terminology. This approach also effectively exploits rich acoustic semantics that are often lost during intermediate text generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RSTalker achieves state-of-the-art localization accuracy and noise robustness. Notably, by eliminating manual data entry and heavy decoder stacks, the proposed paradigm delivers a  $3.5\times $  speedup in complete interaction-to-inference time compared to conventional text-based baselines. This paves the way for intuitive, hands-free interaction in urgent remote sensing tasks.
author: Yaoyong Liu, Yue Zhou, Xue Yang

title: High-Resolution Migration With Stable SVD-Based Inverse Hessian Compensation
content: Conventional Kirchhoff migration is commonly affected by limited resolution, reflector broadening, and sidelobe contamination. Here, we propose DSVD-IHCM, a migration-imaging method that uses singular-value decomposition-based damped inverse Hessian compensation. The method first constructs local point-spread functions (PSFs) from the migration responses of scattering points and then explicitly forms an image-domain Hessian by spatial interpolation. A stable inverse Hessian operator is then constructed by applying damping to the singular-value inverse and is applied to the conventional migration image to reduce blurring and improve resolution. To avoid the memory and computational burden associated with explicit storage and global inversion of the full Hessian, we use blockwise construction, blockwise inversion, and weighted stitching. Experiments with a horizontally layered model, the Marmousi model, and field seismic data show that the constructed Hessian captures the Kirchhoff migration response. Compared with conventional migration and gradient-based image-domain least-squares methods, DSVD-IHCM more effectively compresses the main lobe, suppresses sidelobes and artifacts, and improves reflector focusing and spatial resolution. The method also remains stable and robust for noisy data, providing a practical route to high-resolution image-domain migration compensation.
author: Liwei Song, Yilin Bai, Ying Shi, Ning Wang

title: Toward Practical and Reliable Electromagnetic Inversion: A Semi-Stochastic Lévy Gradient Descent Approach With Trajectory-Based Model Assessment
content: Quantitative assessment of inverted models has long been a major challenge in geophysical inversion, particularly in 3-D electromagnetic (EM) inversion. Traditional gradient-based inversion methods are computationally efficient, but their results strongly depend on the initial model and may converge to local minima. Moreover, they generally provide only a global measure of data misfit, such as the rms, rather than spatially resolved information on the reliability of the recovered model. In contrast, fully stochastic methods can deliver uncertainty estimates through posterior probability distributions, yet their computational cost remains prohibitive for 3-D EM inversion. To bridge this gap, we propose a semi-stochastic inversion algorithm based on the Lévy flight process—Lévy Gradient Descent (LGD). This method utilizes gradient information to guide the search direction and employs the Lévy flight process to generate stochastic step sizes, combining gradient-guided local search with broader stochastic exploration of the parameter space. This enables a more comprehensive and efficient exploration of the solution space. More importantly, the statistical information provided by LGD effectively offers assessments for the inversion results, serving as a crucial complementary metric beyond data misfit for interpreting inverted models. This allows for a relative assessment of the structural stability of individual model parameters in the model. We tested the LGD algorithm on both synthetic and real data. The results demonstrate that LGD produces results comparable or superior to nonlinear conjugate gradient (NLCG), while the trajectory-based structural stability indicator offers valuable insights for interpretation. Our new resistivity model of the Yellowstone hotspot region reveals a deep mantle plume head that appears to connect to shallow structures only through weak, moderately conductive channels—suggesting a waning hotspot.
author: Ziyu Tang, Bo Yang, Yi Zhang

title: FVT: Feature-to-Video Transition Modeling for Semantic Change Detection
content: Semantic change detection aims to identify changed regions and recognize their semantic categories from remote sensing images acquired at two different times. One of the key challenges is to model cross-temporal change relationships effectively. However, most of the existing methods struggle to maintain stable semantic representations in complex cross-temporal scenarios, and the change processes are often treated as discrete. This leads to inconsistent semantic understanding across time and makes it difficult to capture the progressive nature of real-world changes. To further overcome the limitations of existing input-level dynamic change modeling, we propose FVT, a semantic change detection network integrating self-supervised priors with the pair-to-video (P2V) paradigm, explicitly modeling change transitions at the feature level. Specifically, we introduce a P2V-based feature-level temporal evolution strategy transforming bitemporal features into continuous video-like feature sequences. Furthermore, a bidirectional video feature module is designed to characterize directional “from–to” semantic transitions, together with a difference-frame enhancement mechanism to emphasize fine-grained interframe changes. Extensive experiments on the SECOND and Landsat-SCD datasets demonstrate that FVT achieves state-of-the-art performance compared with 12 representative methods.
author: Hao Du, Erming Liu, Xiaochen Zhang, Hao Wang, Jiangyun Li, Tianxiang Zhang

title: Revisiting the Effectiveness of Self-Supervised Learning for Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
content: Remote sensing image change detection is a core task in Earth observation and geographic information science. In recent years, deep learning-based change detection methods have become the mainstream approach. However, these fully supervised methods impose stringent requirements on both the quantity and quality of labeled data. Consequently, self-supervised and unsupervised methods, which reduce or eliminate dependence on manual annotations, have attracted considerable research attention. Nevertheless, this study finds that, within a typical change detection paradigm combining self-supervised pretraining with unsupervised postprocessing, the self-supervised learning process fails to provide effective optimization. Its training behavior is comparable to random initialization and may even lead to performance degradation, exhibiting characteristics of a pseudorandom process. Experiments on the publicly available OSCD and AirChange datasets support this finding. Further analysis shows that self-supervised contrastive change detection methods can still achieve a certain level of performance because their feature extraction network, ResUNet, preserves low-level visual information. We argue that these low-level visual features, rather than the self-supervised learning process itself, are the key factor underlying the effectiveness of this class of methods. To further validate this argument, we replace the feature extraction networks used in the investigated paradigm with a single convolutional layer. This simplified approach achieves the best performance within the examined paradigm, obtaining F1-scores of 0.529 and 0.263 on the OSCD and AirChange datasets, respectively, outperforming the best-performing baseline on each dataset by 0.2 and 3.5 percentage points.
author: Xian Li, Hang Ruan, Decheng Wang, Chengli Peng, Haifeng Li, Zhenyang Huang

title: Deep Learning and Reflectance Spectroscopy for Mapping Rare Earths in Brazil
content: Found in various rocks and soils, rare earth elements (REEs) are essential to the high-tech industry and the energy transition due to their electrical and magnetic properties. However, identifying and mapping them remains a challenge, often requiring time-consuming chemical analyses and costly techniques. Brazil stands out internationally for its large and diverse rare earth reserves, yet domestic geological knowledge regarding these elements remains limited. Analyzing absorption bands in the reflectance spectra of rocks and soils may enable the identification of constituent minerals and elements, thereby facilitating their characterization and classification. Aiming to develop a tool to assist in the identification and mapping of REEs, this article integrates deep learning techniques with reflectance spectroscopy and orbital hyperspectral imagery to seek a faster, lower-cost solution for mineral prospecting. Using laboratory-measured reflectance spectra from rock, soil, and regolith samples obtained from various Brazilian regions, a multilayer perceptron neural network model was trained to map potential occurrences, while a Hopfield network model was trained for mineral identification. Spectral analysis revealed a predominance of clay minerals, and the prediction algorithm successfully identified mining sites and areas of exposed soil potentially containing REEs concentrations in the order of 144 ppm.
author: Matheus M. Gomes, Ruy M. Castro, Gustavo S. Vieira

title: CA-DSUNet: A Novel Physics-Prior-Guided Dual-Stream Deep Coupling Network for Flood Inundated Area Forecasting in Emergent Support
content: Rapid forecasting of spatiotemporal flood evolution is critical for emergency response. However, traditional hydrodynamic models face computational bottlenecks, while purely data-driven models lack physical constraints, frequently generating topologically implausible overspill in complex terrains. Here we propose CA-DSUNet, a physics-prior-guided dual-stream neural network for inundation forecasting. The architecture uses a lightweight, CPU-based cellular automata (CA) module to compute gravity-driven expansion envelopes from local topography, establishing an antecedent physical boundary. A dual-stream encoder then fuses a five-day historical flood sequence with static topographic constraints to perform nonlinear residual mapping strictly within this prior envelope, balancing hydrodynamic momentum capture with resistance to static-background overfitting. To supervise training, we couple signed distance fields with Otsu adaptive thresholding and cumulative precipitation to reconstruct continuous flood trajectories from sparse satellite observations. Evaluated on Poyang Lake and transferred to the East Dongting Lake basin, CA-DSUNet overcomes the identity mapping trap common to time-series models and suppresses disordered overflow. The model achieves an overall intersection over union (IoU) of 0.948 on Poyang Lake and maintains an IoU of 0.990 under cross-basin transfer, while significantly reducing false negatives at highly transient flood frontiers. By bounding deep feature extraction with fundamental physical constraints, this framework provides an accurate, generalizable, and computationally efficient solution for real-time flood forecasting.
author: Zheng Zhou, Jianzhong Lu, Mengfan Li, Shoujing Yin, Liqiong Chen, Xiaoling Chen

title: Efficient On-Board Processing of Oblique AAV Video for Rapid Flood Extent Mapping
content: Effective disaster response relies on rapid situational awareness, where oblique aerial video is the primary modality for initial scouting due to its ability to maximize spatial coverage and situational awareness in limited flight time. However, the on-board processing of high-resolution oblique streams is severely bottlenecked by the strict size, weight, and power constraints of autonomous aerial vehicles (AAVs). The computational density required to process these wide-field-of-view streams precludes low-latency inference on standard edge hardware. To address this, we propose temporal token reuse (TTR), an adaptive inference framework capable of accelerating video segmentation on embedded devices. TTR exploits the intrinsic spatiotemporal redundancy of aerial video by formulating image patches as tokens; it utilizes a lightweight similarity metric to dynamically identify static regions and propagate their precomputed deep features, thereby bypassing redundant backbone computations. We validate the framework on standard benchmarks and a newly curated Oblique Floodwater Dataset designed for hydrological monitoring. Experimental results on edge-grade hardware demonstrate that TTR achieves speedups ranging from 1.58× to 1.69× on video datasets (Floodwater, AAVid, Audi Autonomous Driving Dataset) with negligible degradation in segmentation accuracy ($< $1% mean intersection over union). On the image-based FloodNet benchmark, where temporal redundancy is inherently absent, TTR preserves full accuracy without degradation. These findings confirm that TTR effectively shifts the operational Pareto frontier for oblique video understanding, with the magnitude of efficiency gains scaling directly with the degree of temporal redundancy present in the input stream.
author: Vishisht Sharma, Sam Leroux, Lisa Landuyt, Nick Witvrouwen, Pieter Simoens

title: Water Vapor Pressure Profile Retrieval From GNSS Radio Occultation Without NWP Background Fields During Inference Using a Decoupled Cross-Attention Network
content: Global navigation satellite system (GNSS) radio occultation (RO) water vapor pressure retrieval commonly adopts 1-D variational assimilation. This method relies on numerical weather prediction (NWP) background fields and can be limited by degraded background quality, missing background data, or the need for near-real-time processing. Data-driven retrieval methods provide a possible complementary approach that avoids the use of event-specific NWP background profiles during inference. However, existing studies mostly focus on conventional machine learning models, and the modeling of the vertical structure of refractivity and environmental contextual information remains insufficient. To this end, this article proposes a Decoupled Cross-Attention Network (DCA-Net), which directly retrieves water vapor pressure profiles using refractivity profiles and a limited number of environmental context variables as inputs. DCA-Net first decomposes the refractivity profile into a trend component representing large-scale variations and a disturbance component representing local detailed variations through a high-low frequency decomposition module. Subsequently, differentiated convolutional encoding branches are used to extract the vertical structural features of the two components, and an environment-guided cross-attention mechanism is employed to model the adaptive interaction among trend features, disturbance features, and environmental context features, thereby reconstructing the water vapor pressure profile. Experiments based on COSMIC-2, ERA5, and integrated global radiosonde archive radiosonde observations show that DCA-Net achieves competitive retrieval performance among multiple data-driven methods, providing a feasible complementary scheme for GNSS RO water vapor pressure profile retrieval when real-time high-quality background fields are unavailable or degraded.
author: Qian Gao, Anxin Li, Chun Hu, Dezhi Zheng

title: TempLocate: Endpoint-Supervised Temporal Change Localization for Time-Series Change Detection
content: Time-series remote sensing change detection usually requires pixel-level annotations for every adjacent temporal interval, resulting in high annotation costs. We instead consider a temporal-weakly supervised setting in which only endpoint annotations are available during training. Under this setting, we propose TempLocate, a framework that identifies change intervals from endpoint supervision. Given a remote sensing image sequence, TempLocate first extracts multiscale spatial features and refines them with an intrinsic spatial feature refinement (ISFR) module. By suppressing appearance variations caused by illumination and seasonal changes, ISFR learns more discriminative intrinsic features for subsequent change analysis. Based on the refined features, adjacent and endpoint differences are constructed to characterize local and global changes, respectively. The proposed global-to-local change calibration module then uses the endpoint difference to calibrate adjacent differences, allowing endpoint supervision to be effectively transferred to intermediate temporal intervals. During training, only endpoint annotations are required. To compensate for the lack of intermediate supervision, changed and unchanged consistency constraints are introduced to encourage accurate identification of change intervals. Extensive experiments on two global-scale benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of TempLocate. The proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches and even surpasses fully supervised time-series change detection methods, achieving F1-score improvements of 1.88% and 1.75% on DynamicEarthNet and SpaceNet7, respectively.
author: Jialu Li, Fulin Luo, Chuan Fu, Chen Wu

title: Detection of Oil Spills in Simulated Coastal Marine Environments via Hyperspectral Imaging and 3-D CNN
content: The early detection and classification of oil spills in the ocean is crucial to mitigate potential harm to the environment and economy. Optical hyperspectral remote sensing is an effective method for monitoring and tracking these events, primarily because of the high spectral precision and the possibility of multiscale spatial coverage. Despite the great potential of these sensors, the detection of ocean oil spills through optical images, especially in coastal environments, still requires human interpretation, delaying response efforts. Accurately measuring oil spill thickness is crucial for understanding the incident and its impacts. However, it remains a challenge due to limited studies, scarce data, and unreliable measurement techniques. A promising approach to automating hyperspectral imaging processing is utilizing deep learning models. This research evaluates the effectiveness of 3-D convolutional neural networks in detecting and classifying oil spill thickness through hyperspectral imaging in the visible/near-infrared and short-wave infrared regions. The data used to train the model were acquired through a controlled field experiment in which oil spills were simulated under conditions similar to marine coastal environments. Savitzky–Golay filters and continuous wavelet signal decomposition were applied in data preprocessing before the application of a 3-D convolutional neural network. The combination of continuous wavelet analysis and 3-D convolutional neural networks proved to be a promising approach to identify and estimate oil spill thickness on hyperspectral data, achieving an overall accuracy of 97.85%, a Kappa coefficient of 0.96, and a weighted F1-score of 0.98. This provides a scalable and accurate approach for early response to oil spill monitoring in coastal environments.
author: Thassia Pine Gondek, Carlos Roberto de Souza Filho, Lucas de Paula Miranda, Guillaume Lassalle, Rebecca Del Papa Moreira Scafutto

title: Improving Forest Canopy Cover Mapping Through ICESat-2-Derived Understory DEM and Multisource Remote Sensing Data
content: Canopy cover (CC) is a key indicator of forest horizontal structure. However, in regional-scale forest environments, the spatial heterogeneity of canopy structure, limitations of understory DEMs, and differences in multisource remote sensing responses may still affect the stability and accuracy of CC estimation. This study developed a regional-scale CC estimation framework by integrating ICESat-2 ATL08 samples, random forest-derived digital elevation model (RFDEM), Sentinel-1 C-band and ALOS-2 PALSAR-2 L-band SAR observations, Landsat-9 optical features, forest canopy height (FHC), and land-cover information using a Bayesian optimization-based random forest (BO-RF) model. The framework was evaluated in Georgia, Maryland, and South Carolina and independently validated using G-LiHT airborne LiDAR data. The results show that RFDEM provides a more reliable representation of understory terrain than forest and buildings removed copernicus digital elevation model (FABDEM) in forested areas, with DTM RMSE values of 3.080, 2.308, and 2.221 m in Georgia, Maryland, and South Carolina, respectively, compared with 3.861, 9.507, and 4.478 m for FABDEM. Compared with the FABDEM-based BO-RF models, the RFDEM-based BO-RF models improved test $R^{2}$ and reduced test RMSE in all three study areas. The final BO-RF model achieved $R^{2}$ values of 0.889, 0.893, and 0.892 in Georgia, Maryland, and South Carolina, respectively, during model validation, and maintained $R^{2}$ values of 0.728, 0.796, and 0.755 in independent validation. Feature-combination experiments and SHAP analysis indicate that L-band SAR, FHC, and RFDEM variables provided important information for CC estimation, with their relative importance varying among the three study areas. Overall, the results suggest that combining understory terrain information with optical, SAR, and structural features can improve regional-scale CC estimation under the tested conditions.
author: Mengyao Wang, Jiapeng Huang, Tao Zheng

title: Dynamic Priority Replay and Boundary-Aware Distillation for Remote Sensing Scene Domain Incremental Classification
content: The continuous growth of remote sensing imagery introduces substantial distribution discrepancies between previously observed and newly acquired domains, making remote sensing scene classification models susceptible to catastrophic forgetting during domain-incremental learning. To address this challenge, this article proposes a dynamic priority replay and boundary-aware distillation (DPR-BAD) framework. Specifically, a dynamic priority metric is designed by jointly exploiting cross-domain semantic shifts and prediction entropy to identify highly informative historical samples for replay, thereby improving knowledge retention under cross-domain feature distribution shifts. Furthermore, a BAD strategy is introduced to adaptively adjust the distillation strength according to each sample’s contribution to decision boundary stability, enabling stronger preservation of boundary-critical knowledge while alleviating forgetting of previously learned domains. Extensive experiments on four publicly available remote sensing scene classification datasets demonstrate that DPR-BAD consistently outperforms representative continual learning methods, achieving an average accuracy of 93.02% while effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting without compromising adaptation to new domains.
author: Jian Hu, Xue Li

title: DAC-Net: Divide-and-Conquer Network for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) plays a vital role in remote sensing and automated early-warning infrastructure. However, its performance is deeply constrained by the dim nature of targets and complex background clutter. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have driven advancements in this field, they often struggle to capture global contextual information, leading to an inaccurate understanding of background semantics and triggering false alarms. Meanwhile, existing methods overlook the physical and morphological characteristics of the targets themselves, which can easily lead to boundary distortion and missed detections. To resolve these limitations, we propose a novel network based on a hybrid architecture, named DAC-Net. Specifically, we introduce the Edge-aware CNN-VMamba Fusion module into the encoder, which adopts a CNN-VMamba dual-branch structure to thoroughly learn both local details and global semantics. To enhance the network’s representation capability for the IRSTD task, a dynamic multiscale enhancement module is incorporated to effectively capture the physical and morphological characteristics of targets across diverse scales, achieving further feature selection and background suppression. Furthermore, an explicit edge loss is integrated into the joint optimization framework to supervise boundary gradient variations, thereby alleviating target shape distortion. Extensive experiments on NUAA-SIRST, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1K datasets demonstrate that our proposed DAC-Net outperforms existing methods across various evaluation metrics.
author: Zhengyi Huang, Dawei Ren, Yan Zhang, Yongsheng Xie, Jianpo Liu

title: Large-Scale Quantum Kernels for Hyperspectral Data Classification
content: Quantum kernel methods have emerged as a promising approach for leveraging high-dimensional feature spaces in machine learning, particularly in domains where classical kernel methods face scalability limitations. In this work, we present the first large-scale study of fidelity-quantum-kernel support vector machines for hyperspectral data classification without requiring heavy prior feature selection or dimensionality reduction. By simulating quantum kernels using tensor network contraction techniques and graphics processing unit acceleration, we overcome the computational bottlenecks traditionally associated with quantum models, achieving quadratic scaling $O(n^{2})$ in the number of qubits. Our approach enables the evaluation of quantum kernels on hyperspectral data with hundreds of spectral bands, aligning quantum feature spaces with real-world remote sensing applications. We provide an in-depth analysis of kernel bandwidth optimization, demonstrating its crucial role in mitigating exponential concentration effects and ensuring the model's ability to generalize. Experimental results on binary classification (Indian Pines and methane detection) and multiclass classification (Indian Pines) demonstrate that quantum kernels achieve competitive performance compared to a broad range of state-of-the-art classical baselines. As illustrative cases, on four 50-band splits selected from Indian Pines, the quantum model achieved a $78.0 \pm 6.2$% accuracy for a binary classification task compared to $72.0 \pm 5.0$% for the standard radial basis function kernel. For a four-class classification task, the quantum kernel reached $83.3 \pm 3.1$% accuracy, outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines. On five 75-band splits selected from the methane detection dataset, the quantum approach yielded $58.5 \pm 5.0$% accuracy versus $55.1 \pm 2.5$% for the classical counterpart. This study provides a foundation for future exploration of quantum machine learning in high-dimensional Earth observation tasks.
author: Amer Delilbasic, Artur Miroszewski, Agata M. Wijata, Jakub Nalepa, Jakub Mielczarek, Morris Riedel, Gabriele Cavallaro

title: MDCF-Net: Multiscale Dual-Domain Collaborative-Aware Feature Fusion Network for Hyperspectral and Multispectral Image Fusion
content: Deep learning-based image fusion methods have achieved remarkable progress in the fusion task of low-resolution hyperspectral images (LR-HSI) and high-resolution multispectral images (HR-MSI). However, existing solutions still suffer from limitations, particularly in multiscale feature representation and cross-scale information fusion. To resolve these limitations, we propose a multiscale dual-domain collaborative-aware feature fusion network (MDCF-Net) for LR-HSI and HR-MSI fusion. To overcome the insufficiency of multiscale feature representation, MDCF-Net extracts features by constructing a multiscale patch-based dual-domain feature extraction (MPDFE) module. Specifically, the MPDFE module employs dual-domain feature extraction (DDFE) modules with varying receptive fields to capture multiscale spatial and frequency information from source images. The DDFE module consists of a spatial feature extraction module and a frequency feature extraction module, which jointly exploit fine-grained spatial information and global frequency distribution characteristics through deep convolution and Fourier transform. By leveraging the complementarity between spatial and frequency domains, the model enhances the completeness and discriminability of fused features, thereby providing more expressive intermediate representations for subsequent cross-scale feature fusion. Furthermore, to resolve the issue of insufficient cross-scale information integration, we build a dual-domain collaborative perception fusion module. This module enables adaptive weighted combination of spatial and frequency-domain features at multiple scales, significantly improving the model’s joint representation ability. Evaluations on three simulated datasets and one real dataset show that our approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative scores and subjective visual quality under various scenarios.
author: Shuaiqi Liu, Huanru Yue, Zezheng Zhang, Bing Li, Qi Hu, Cong Liu, Siyuan Liu

title: A Review of Hyperspectral Unmixing Considering Spectral Variability
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is a fundamental task in the analysis and interpretation of hyperspectral images. A large number of HU methods have been developed rapidly, and several review papers have summarized these developments. More recently, spectral variability (SV) has attracted increasing attention in HU, leading to the emergence of various SV-aware hyperspectral unmixing (SVHU) methods. While existing reviews cover general HU, dedicated surveys on SVHU remain scarce. Moreover, most relevant reviews focus on a specific methodological branch and fail to address the latest advances. To address this gap, we present a comprehensive review of SVHU methods. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this is the first work to propose a unified SVHU framework that covers both single-temporal and multitemporal settings. Existing SVHU methods are systematically categorized into three groups: model-driven, data-driven, and model–data-driven approaches, each of which is discussed in detail. Subsequently, we describe the datasets and evaluation metrics, and compare several representative state-of-the-art methods on multiple commonly used public datasets. In addition, we summarize related downstream applications, including hyperspectral super-resolution, classification, and change detection. Finally, we discuss the main challenges and outline several promising directions for future research.
author: Jianing Huang, Hui Li, Jiayi Li, Zebin Wu, Danfeng Hong, Hongyi Liu, Zhihui Wei

title: Benchmarking Hyperspectral Transfer and Graph Learning for Coastal Water-Quality and Anomaly Mapping With PACE OCI
content: Monitoring water quality in optically complex coastal seas is limited by sparse in-situ sampling, short hyper-spectral satellite records, and retrieval algorithms that transfer poorly across sensors under label scarcity. We address these for the English Channel with a spectral-transfer, benchmarking, graph-learning, and cross-sensor framework built on NASA PACE OCI reflectance (340–895 nm, 5 nm), whose sub-two-year record cannot alone support climatological assessment. PACE spectra are matched to the GLORIA in-situ library through $k$-nearest-neighbour cosine similarity to estimate chlorophyll-$a$ (Chl-$a$), total suspended solids (TSS), and CDOM absorption $a_{\mathrm{CDOM}}(440)$; spectral-angle, cosine, and normalized-RMSE diagnostics flag analogue reliability. This prior is fused with PACE band descriptors, lagged MODIS observations, ERA5/CHIR PS forcing, and station-graph connectivity in a benchmark of persistence, ridge regression, tree ensembles, stacked ensembles, and graph neural networks. On a held-out 2025 split across 32 monitoring nodes, tree ensembles are the strongest predictors: Extra-Trees reaches $R^{2}\!=\!0.94$ for Chl-$a$ and lifts $a_{dg}(442)$ from 0.17 to 0.39 (Diebold--Mariano $p\!<\!0.01$), while XGBoost reaches $R^{2}\!=\!0.94$ for particulate organic carbon. Persistence remains best for normalized fluorescence line height; standalone graph networks under-perform under label scarcity, but the adaptive graph encoder supplies spatially coherent dense-grid inference with per-pixel uncertainty. Predictive uncertainty tracks held-out absolute error for Chl-$a$ (Spearman $\rho\!=\!0.80$), supporting per-pixel quality flagging. A gradient-boosted MODIS-to-PACE bridge for $b_{bp}(442)$ (cross-validated $R^{2}\!=\!0.61, r\!=\!0.78$, $n\!=\!267$) provides 2012–2025 particle-load context; spring 2025 is the strongest seasonal departure in the 14-year archive (13.7 % of pixels with $|z|\!>\!2$). Station validation, grid inference, spectral-library consistency, and cross-sensor extrapolation remain separate evidence levels with explicit claim boundaries.
author: Abhinav Galodha, Maria Valasia Peppa, Sanya Anees, Brejesh Lall, Shaikh Ziauddin Ahammad

title: Beyond Linear Convolutional Representations: Manifold-Aware Neighborhood Feature Learning for PolSAR Ship Detection
content: Classical polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) ship detectors can be unified into a quadratic form of polarimetric scattering vectors, offering clear physical interpretability. To further exploit spatial information, the neighborhood polarimetric covariance matrix (NPCM) was introduced to characterize inter-pixel polarimetric coherences. However, NPCM-based approaches fundamentally rely on single-look complex data and suffer from high computational complexity, limiting their applicability in large-scale multilook scenarios. Conversely, convolutional neural networks have become a dominant paradigm but are often treated as “black boxes” operating in Euclidean space. A fundamental theoretical gap remains: for the pre-activation, single-layer linear convolutional representation analyzed in this article, the corresponding function class is a strict subset of the NPCM function class. This result shows that such linear convolutional aggregation cannot represent the off-diagonal inter-pixel correlation terms captured by NPCM, especially when phase information is absent. To bridge this gap, a manifold-aware neighborhood feature learning framework is proposed. Instead of treating polarimetric matrices as flat vectors in Euclidean space, the Riemannian geometric structure of polarimetric covariance matrices is explicitly embedded into the network representation. By constructing a neighborhood quadratic embedding, nonlinear inter-pixel polarimetric interactions are effectively learned from incoherent multilook data, acting as a proxy for the missing phase information. Experiments on both simulated and measured datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms standard linear convolutional representations.
author: Ziyuan Yang, Peng Zhang, Yao Yao, Liguo Liu, Yinghui Quan, Tao Liu

title: Few-Shot Hyperspectral Image Classification: A Review of Deep Architectures, Paradigms, and Benchmarks
content: The critical bottleneck in hyperspectral image (HSI) classification lies in the inherent conflict between the extreme scarcity of labeled samples and the massive data requirements of deep models, making few-shot classification a vital research frontier. This article presents a comprehensive review of recent advances in deep learning for few-shot HSI classification, systematically structured around core architectures, learning paradigms, and rigorous benchmarking. At the architectural level, we trace the evolutionary trajectory from traditional convolutional neural networks to global-modeling Transformers, and further to emerging Mamba models that achieve linear complexity with global receptive fields. Concurrently, from a learning paradigm perspective, we analyze the mechanisms of transfer learning, meta-learning, and contrastive learning in mitigating sample constraints. Crucially, to eliminate pervasive cross-study evaluation biases, we establish a unified benchmark across four public datasets, conducting standardized quantitative cross-validation of three representative architectures and three advanced paradigms. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that long-range dependence models (Transformer and Mamba) exhibit superior generalization under extremely limited samples. Furthermore, contrastive and transfer learning paradigms significantly expand interclass feature margins, enhancing overall model robustness. Finally, we outline promising future directions, including physics-informed deep learning, frequency-aware reconstruction, and multilevel semantic enhancement for complex cross-domain scenarios.
author: Qiyuan Wang, Shuo Zhang, Feifei Yang, Yu Huan, Jianfeng Jia, Weishuo Li, Dazhong Liu

title: PGTFusion: Progressive Group-Feature Transmission Fusion Network for Pansharpening
content: Pansharpening aims to obtain multispectral images with high-spatial resolution (HRMS) by fusing high-spatial-resolution panchromatic (PAN) images with low-spatial-resolution multispectral (LRMS) images. Most deep learning-based methods directly extract all band features of LRMS images and fuse them with PAN image features to reconstruct HRMS, which leads to inaccurate feature reconstruction for each band. To address this issue, we propose a progressive group-feature transmission fusion network (PGTFusion) with a multiscale and multibranch structure for pansharpening to achieve the extraction and fusion of different group features at different scales. At the minimum scale layer, considering the correlation between adjacent band features in LRMS images, a group-feature extraction transmission block (GETB) is designed to extract and fuse features from adjacent bands to obtain the group features, which were then transmitted to adjacent group for feature supplementation. At the intermediate scale layer, a group-feature fusion transmission block (GFTB) is constructed to achieve the fusion of group features and PAN images features, and the fused features are transferred to adjacent group to enhance the group features. At the maximum scale layer, a spatial information block (SIB) is utilized to achieve precise fusion of group features and PAN images features. Numerous experiments conducted on simulated and real datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms some state-of-the-art methods in both subjective and objective evaluation.
author: Dongping Huang, Yong Yang, Shuying Huang, Xiaozheng Wang, Shuxia Ren

title: From Coseismic Disturbance to Short-Term Dynamic Recovery: Nighttime Light Perspective on the Disaster Response to the Myanmar Mw 7.7 Earthquake
content: Nighttime light (NTL) remote sensing effectively captures urban human activities and socioeconomic dynamics, offering a novel observational approach for earthquake impact assessment. However, existing studies have predominantly focused on either immediate postseismic losses or long-term recovery processes, with insufficient attention to the dynamic characteristics of the critical recovery period spanning from days to weeks after an earthquake. Taking the Myanmar Mw 7.7 earthquake of 28 March 2025 as a case study, this study constructed a preseismic NTL baseline and the NTL change rate index based on black marble NTL data to investigate coseismic urban light disturbances and the recovery process during the month following the earthquake. The results show that approximately 70% of urban patches experienced coseismic NTL attenuation, with nearly half showing a reduction of more than 50%. The degree of NTL attenuation generally decreased with increasing distance from the epicenter and exhibited good correspondence with seismic intensity. Using a dynamic threshold method, 51 areas with anomalous NTL declines were further identified. Their postseismic recovery process was generally characterized by rapid recovery in the early stage followed by a gradual transition to a stable recovery state, while recovery trajectories exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity among different regions. Based on NTL time-series analysis, three typical recovery patterns were identified: rapid-stable recovery, fluctuating recovery, and delayed recovery, whose spatial distributions showed good agreement with seismic intensity levels. The findings demonstrate that NTL remote sensing cannot only effectively identify the immediate impacts of earthquakes but also characterize the dynamic evolution of the critical postseismic recovery stage, providing valuable technical support for postdisaster recovery monitoring and urban resilience assessment.
