Scattering keypoint automatic annotation (SKAA) automatically generates attributed scattering center (ASC)-based keypoint annotations, scattering topology injection module (STIM) injects the learned topology into multiscale features, and scattering prior supervision strategy (SPSS) uses Gaussian soft targets to supervise the scattering-map branch. Across seven convolutional neural network (CNN)-, Transformer-, and Mamba-based detectors, PASTE yields relative mean average precision (mAP)@0.5 gains of 1.3%–11.3%. Visualizations further show that the learned scattering representations distinguish target and background regions, improving interpretability together with detection accuracy. In addition, parameter ablation experiments and robustness perturbation experiments are also conducted to verify the practicality of PASTE.
author: Jiacheng Chen, Yuxuan Xiong, Haipeng Wang

title: WaveDSNet: A Wavelet-Enhanced Discrepancy Semantic Network for Water Change Detection in SAR Imagery
content: Water change detection in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery is important for inundation extent delineation and river course monitoring. However, existing methods still face three core challenges: inherent speckle noise interference, insufficient extraction of semantic-structural features, and the lack of dedicated benchmarks for evaluating high-resolution structural details. To address these issues, a wavelet-enhanced discrepancy semantic network (WaveDSNet) and the Xidian University SAR Water Change Detection (XDU-SWCD) dataset are proposed for water change detection in SAR imagery. WaveDSNet consists of two key components: first, a wavelet-based noise suppression (WNS)-embedded backbone performs wavelet-subband-aware denoising to suppress speckle while preserving structural cues; second, a semantic-boundary collaborative refinement (SBCR) module aggregates bi-temporal features into difference and semantic streams, and further coordinates them through bidirectional interaction and adaptive gating, with auxiliary boundary-aware supervision for fine-grained changed-water boundary localization. Furthermore, the XDU-SWCD dataset is constructed as a focused high-resolution benchmark for SAR water change detection. It combines fine-grained water-change structures with representative confusing nonwater regions, enabling a rigorous evaluation of boundary delineation and robustness to low-backscatter pseudo-changes. The experiments on XDU-SWCD show that WaveDSNet achieves stronger overall performance than nine representative change detection methods, with an overall IoU of 0.7796 and an overall  ${F}1$ -score of 0.8590. Zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation on public benchmarks further demonstrates its promising transferability. These results suggest the effectiveness of both the proposed framework and the XDU-SWCD benchmark for SAR water change detection. Our code and XDU-SWCD dataset will be publicly available at https://github.com/gosling123456/WaveDSNet.git
author: Shulin Gao, Zhongle Ren, Kai Wang, Guangyao Feng, Xi Li, Weicheng Zang, Biao Hou, Weibin Li, Licheng Jiao

title: Frequency-Aware Bias Calibration Attention Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Recently, self-attention mechanisms have significantly advanced hyperspectral image classification (HSIC) by enabling effective modeling of long-range spatial–spectral dependencies. However, existing methods often suffer from blurred land-cover boundaries and insufficient discriminability between spectrally similar classes due to redundant global interactions and inadequate preservation of fine-grained spatial details. To address these challenges, we propose a novel frequency-aware bias calibration attention network (FBCANet) for HSIC. Specifically, we design a frequency-domain spatial–spectral global aggregation module to model global contextual dependencies in the frequency domain. Within this module, a global frequency enhancement filter (GFEF) explicitly decouples complex frequency representations to adaptively suppress redundant interference caused by similar spectral signatures across different categories. Furthermore, we introduce a bias-calibrated global attention (BCGA) module, which compensates for the representation bias introduced by global attention modeling. This module consists of a global feature aggregation backbone and an explicit bias-calibration branch that extracts fine-grained spatial–spectral cues and injects them into the global interaction process, thereby enhancing interclass discriminability. In addition, a dual-path frequency-aware interaction module is proposed to capture high-frequency information and dynamically compensate for the loss of detailed textures and complex land-cover boundaries. Extensive experiments on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that the proposed method learns highly discriminative feature representations and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art HSIC methods. The source code for this work will be publicly available at https://github.com/szq0816/FBCANet
author: Zhenqiu Shu, Nanbo Liu, Kexin Zeng, Hongbin Wang, Jun Zhou

title: MDFPF-Net: Multidomain Feature Perceptual Fusion Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) is crucial for retrieving subpixel information. However, existing deep learning (DL) methods typically rely on original spatial–spectral information and struggle to fuse the complementary advantages of multidomain features, resulting in endmember confusion and inaccurate abundance estimation. To address these challenges, a multidomain feature perceptual fusion network (MDFPF-Net) is proposed for HU. The network constructs a parallel feature extraction framework across the spatial, spectral, and frequency domains. Specifically, the spatial–spectral feature extraction (SSFE) module adopts a dual-branch design to capture distinct spatial and spectral attributes, while a frequency-domain multibranch attention (FMBA) module is introduced to selectively suppress redundant responses and enhance frequency components with stronger separability under the guidance of fine-grained texture information, yielding a high-fidelity representation of material distributions. To enhance cross-domain complementarity, a cross-domain dynamic perception (CDDP) module is designed. It uses adaptive context-aware convolutional kernels to achieve semantic alignment and collaborative optimization between both spatial–spectral and spatial–frequency features, strengthening endmember spectral discriminability and accurately characterizing abundance distribution discrepancies. Then, learnable parameters are used to adaptively integrate the dual-path outputs, producing deeply fused multidomain features. Finally, a semantic-enhanced abundance generator (SEAG) is embedded within a Transformer encoder–decoder architecture. Endmember-wise collaborative attention enhancement together with lightweight constraints is applied to further improve unmixing accuracy. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that MDFPF-Net achieves superior performance, yielding lower root-mean-square error (RMSE) and spectral angle distance (SAD) than state-of-the-art methods in most cases. The source code is available at https://github.com/Nuist-HSI-Group/MDFPF-Net
author: Xiaocong Wu, Le Sun, Guoqing Zhang, Yadang Chen, Zebin Wu

title: DEViCo: Discriminative Evidence View Correspondence Learning for Drone-Satellite Cross-View Geo-Localization
content: The core objective of cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) is to determine the location of a query image by retrieving its geographically corresponding reference image from a geo-tagged database. A fundamental challenge stems from substantial appearance and geometric discrepancies induced by the distinct imaging geometries of near-nadir satellite imagery and lower altitude oblique drone imagery. Under uniform full image feature extraction, discriminative evidence can be highly intermixed with view-specific contextual regions in the learned representations. To address this, we propose DEViCo: discriminative evidence view (DEV) correspondence learning for drone–satellite CVGL, which constructs a drone-side DEV and introduces a triview dual correspondence learning framework for drone–satellite matching. In particular, a Cross-View Semantic Consistency Attention Generation Module (CAGM) exploits cross-view semantic consistency to generate attention heatmaps that highlight discriminative evidence in drone images. A Discriminative Evidence View Construction Module (DEVCM) then adaptively processes these heatmaps to construct a compact and coherent DEV. Based on the original satellite view, original drone view, and drone DEV, DEViCo performs triview dual correspondence learning, with one correspondence preserving global context and the other emphasizing discriminative evidence. Importantly, DEViCo can be integrated with most visual backbones without modifying their internal architectures. Extensive experiments on University-1652 and SUES-200 demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple backbones, and DEViCo further boosts MEAN to achieve 96.72 R@1 on University-1652 and competitive state-of-the-art-level performance on both benchmarks.
author: Zhixue Yang, Yuehai Chen, Jing Yang, Shaoyi Du, Badong Chen

title: DFS-Mamba: A Dual-Frequency Synergistic Mamba for Cloud Removal in Optical Remote Sensing Images
content: Cloud contamination is a persistent obstacle in optical remote sensing because it obscures surface observations and degrades the reliability of downstream interpretation. Recent diffusion-based and state-space-based methods have improved cloud removal performance, but most of them process cloud-contaminated features in a uniform manner and therefore insufficiently distinguish low-frequency cloud degradation from high-frequency surface details. In this article, we formulate single-image optical cloud removal as a frequency-conditioned state-space restoration problem and propose Dual-Frequency Synergistic Mamba (DFS-Mamba). The core component is a Dual-Frequency Synergistic State Space Layer (DFS-SSL), which first decomposes input features into edge-preserving low-frequency structures and residual high-frequency details through a learnable guided filtering operator. The two components are then restored by branch-specific state-space pathways: a differential-convolution-enhanced high-frequency branch for local texture and boundary recovery, and a Fourier residual low-frequency branch for global cloud-pattern suppression and structural consistency. Finally, an adaptive branch-fusion mechanism recombines the restored components according to their global reliability. Experiments on the RICE1 and RICE2 datasets show that, among the compared methods, DFS-Mamba obtains the highest peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) together with better visual fidelity. We further report the parameter number, MACs/FLOPs, memory footprint, and inference latency of all methods in order to characterize the accuracy–efficiency tradeoff of the proposed model.
author: Xinyi Wang, Yanbo Mai, Shao Deng, Shanzhu Xiao, Huamin Tao, Ping Wang, Zhiyong Song, Li Liu

title: CSTANet: Cross-Frame Spatio-Temporal Aggregation Network for Moving Small-Object Detection in Satellite Videos
content: With the rapid advancement of satellite video technology, detecting small moving objects in satellite videos has shown substantial application potential across domains such as military surveillance, traffic monitoring, and disaster management. However, achieving robust detection remains challenging due to three key factors: 1) limited spatial resolution; 2) complex and dynamic backgrounds; and 3) low object-background contrast. To address these issues, we propose a cross-frame spatio-temporal aggregation network (CSTANet), which deeply exploits and effectively fuses spatio-temporal features to enhance detection accuracy and robustness. Extensive experiments conducted on satellite video moving object detection (MOD) datasets demonstrate that CSTANet outperforms state-of-the-art methods in multiple metrics, including recall, precision, and  $F1$ -score. This study provides an effective solution for detecting small moving objects in satellite videos and is expected to advance the development of downstream remote sensing surveillance missions.
author: Xinrui Qi, Siqian He, Wuzhuo Yang, Yuzeng Chen, Xin Su, Qiangqiang Yuan

title: Quantifying the Effect of Topographic Normalization on Airborne LiDAR-Derived Individual Tree Parameters: A Unified Theoretical–Experimental Framework
content: Airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is widely used to retrieve individual tree parameters (ITPs), including tree height (TH), crown base height (CBH), crown length (CL), and crown volume (CV). However, pointwise topographic normalization over sloping terrain may deform crown geometry and introduce systematic bias. This study develops a first-order, geometry-based analytical framework to quantify topographic normalization-induced biases in TH, CBH, CL, and geometry-defined CV. Using idealized crown geometries and a crown-scale planar terrain approximation, the derived equations relate parameter-specific biases to local terrain slope, equivalent crown radius, crown angle, and crown type. The framework was evaluated using 3000 simulated trees and two airborne LiDAR datasets with contrasting forest structures and point densities. The results showed that topographic normalization generally underestimated CBH and overestimated TH, CL, and CV. Bias magnitude increased with terrain slope and crown radius and generally decreased with crown angle, with responses varying among crown types. The simulated point clouds showed close agreement with the analytical predictions under the prescribed geometric conditions. In both real datasets, the directions and variations of the observed errors were broadly consistent with the predicted normalization-induced bias patterns under the evaluated conditions. Point density analysis showed that sparse sampling reduced agreement with continuous-surface predictions, whereas denser sampling more completely represented crown extrema and boundaries. The analytical relationships were further formulated as a postnormalization correction module without modifying upstream LiDAR processing. The framework estimates the geometric component of topographic normalization-induced error and is most applicable to reliably segmented trees with compact, approximately axisymmetric crowns on locally planar terrain. Greater caution is required for irregular or overlapping crowns, nonplanar terrain, and CV estimation.
author: Sheng Nie, Cheng Wang, Xiaohuan Xi, Xiaoxiao Zhu, Jieying Lao, Shaobo Xia, Zhou Yang, Zijia Wang, Jianyang Chang, Jianan Yu

title: PFDiff: Physics- and Frequency-Guided Residual Diffusion for Remote Sensing Image Dehazing
content: Haze, aerosols, and thin cloud-like atmospheric interference reduce contrast and obscure structural cues in optical remote sensing images, degrading both visual quality and downstream interpretation. Direct-regression networks may not sufficiently exploit physically interpretable haze and frequency cues, whereas full-image diffusion requires iterative reconstruction of the complete clean image. This article presents PFDiff, a physics- and frequency-guided residual diffusion framework for remote sensing image dehazing. A haze-aware restoration U-Net first predicts a coarse restoration using a dark-channel map, a transmission-like proxy, and a Laplacian high-frequency cue. Conditional diffusion then models the lower energy residual between the clean target and the coarse output, conditioned on an 11-channel tensor comprising the hazy input, coarse restoration, and the three priors. A learned gate applies spatially varying residual fusion. We further construct HazeRS45 using real-haze-derived masks, multiple transmission patterns, and atmospheric-light variations. Experiments on paired remote sensing dehazing datasets, a cross-degradation benchmark, unpaired real-world images, and downstream tasks demonstrate strong fidelity and structural preservation. Across RSID and HazeRS45, PFDiff achieves the highest average peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity of 26.17 dB and 0.94, respectively, together with the best average deep image structure and texture similarity among the compared methods. It also shows favorable cross-degradation and no-reference real-world performance. Controlled ablations support the residual target and identify ten-step sampling as a balanced quality–efficiency setting. The source code and dataset are available online.
author: Jianchong Wei, Yan Cao, Dongying Chen, Pingping Chen, Zhensheng Wang, Chengbin Chen

title: Exemplar-Free Lifelong Hyperspectral Image Classification via Dual Constraints and Dynamic Margin Adaptation
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) lifelong classification aims to continuously recognize newly arriving classes while preserving previously acquired knowledge without full model retraining. Although exemplar replay is effective, retaining historical examples is often impractical in real-world applications due to privacy concerns and limited storage resources. Existing exemplar-free methods often suffer from representation drift in feature space and boundary confusion between previous and new classes. To address this issue, we propose an exemplar-free lifelong framework named DC-DMA for HSI classification based on dual-constrained feature extraction (DCFE) and dynamic margin adaptation (DMA). Specifically, DCFE is designed to stabilize spectral–spatial representation learning. It imposes an embedding consistency constraint to preserve low-level spectral–spatial patterns. DCFE also restricts deep parameter updates via the deep orthogonal gradient constraint to protect historical manifolds. Furthermore, to mitigate decision boundary ambiguity, we introduce a classifier with DMA, which maintains online class prototypes to estimate the semantic similarity between previous and new classes and accordingly adjusts class-specific cosine margins, thereby refining decision boundaries. Experiments on Indian Pines, Houston2013, Houston2018, and Hyrank-Loukia show that DC-DMA achieves competitive early-task performance and superior final-task performance against representative continual learning and hyperspectral incremental learning baselines.
author: Jiyang Ma, Haiyang Luo, Shengke Sun, Shengwei Zhong

title: Rethinking Separability Map: A Target-Specified Separability Map for Hyperspectral Target Detection
content: Separability map (SM) is a widely used visualization tool for hyperspectral anomaly detection. It selects a fixed percentile range of [τSM%,100%-τSM%] and then uses it to construct an anomaly box (ax) and a background box (bx), to qualitatively assess anomaly–background separability by visual inspection. Unfortunately, such constructed SM has been erroneously applied to hyperspectral target detection (HTD) mainly because the true targets always produce highest detected target abundances in (100%-τSM%,100%] not [τSM%,100%-τSM%]. To address the issue of ax inapplicably to HTD, a target box (tx) must be constructed directly from HTD, which yields a new notion, called target-specified separability map (TSM) via a single threshold τTSM. Consequently, tx and bx can be correctly constructed by [τTSM%,100%] and [0%,τTSM%] respectively to describe distributions of detected target and background data samples as a qualitative visualization tool. Amazingly, by virtue of TSM, the lengths of these two boxes can be further used to derive three TSM-based quantitatively detection metrics, target-background separation (TSMTBS), TSM-based target detection (TSMTD) and TSM-based BKG suppressibility (TSMBS). This leads to an interesting interpretation for TSM from the Neyman–Pearson detection theory in terms of detection probability, PD and false alarm probability PF where TSMTBS, TSMTD, TSMBS can be considered as counterparts of (PD,PF), (PD,τ), and (PF,τ), respectively. Experimental results demonstrate that SM has been erroneously applied to HTD and TSM can correct this mis-application. Most importantly, TSM can effectively evaluate HTD not only as a qualitative visualization tool but also a quantitative measure.
author: Yuchao Yang, Yulei Wang, Enyu Zhao, Nianxin Qu, Lin Wang, Shuhan Chen, Hongju Cao, Chein-I Chang

title: A Structural Variable-Driven Forest Aboveground Biomass Retrieval Approach Integrating Hybrid Expert Attention and Ecological Priors
content: Accurate estimation of forest aboveground biomass (AGB) is a critical prerequisite for regional carbon accounting. However, existing direct regression methods lack synergistic constraints on the coupling relationships among forest structural variables, such as tree height and diameter at breast height, often causing biomass predictions in complex stands to become homogenized, with systematic underestimation of high values, overestimation of low values, and blurred stand boundaries. To address this, we reframe forest AGB retrieval as a structural variable-driven conditioned mapping problem and propose a hybrid expert attention multitask model (HEAMM). The model employs gated shifted-window self-attention to capture spatial context relevant to forest structure, leverages sparse expert routing in a mixture-of-experts feedforward network (MoE-FFN) to enhance nonlinear mapping capability under diverse local remote-sensing-structure patterns, and constructs an allometric scaling soft constraint based on Repola’s species-specific allometric equations, providing a probabilistic ecological prior to guide the joint prediction of structural variables and AGB estimation. On the Finnish Forest Centre dataset, we established five experimental scenarios: airborne hyperspectral data from TAIGA (0.6 m) and ESSD (0.5 m), AEFORGE-TAIGA and AEFORGE-ESSD based on 10 m spaceborne AlphaEarth embeddings, and RJ-Transfer (a spatially independent test area transfer). HEAMM achieved AGB $R^{2}$ values of 0.915, 0.978, 0.952, 0.961, and 0.824, respectively. Ablation experiments indicate that removing the MoE-FFN led to the most pronounced decline in AGB estimation performance ($-\text{5.1}\%$); the gain from the allometric scaling soft constraint (AEC) ($+\text{5.9}\%$) exceeded that from incorporating canopy height model structural information ($+\text{3.7}\%$), and their combined gain was nearly additive ($+\text{7.3}\%$). Spatial predictions and scatter analysis further reveal that HEAMM effectively alleviates the homogenized outputs typical of direct AGB prediction, producing sharper stand boundaries and more pronounced structural gradients and high–low biomass stratification. The results suggest that joint estimation of structural variables, guided by an allometric probabilistic ecological prior, can simultaneously enhance the numerical accuracy and spatial representation quality of stand-scale AGB retrieval, deliver forest structural parameters and biomass products for complex stands, and provide reliable support for forest carbon stock assessment.
author: Mingda Hao, Yibo Wang, Peijun Du, Jinnian Wang

title: Joint Classification Network via Superpixel-Guided Prototypical Feature for Hyperspectral and LiDAR Data
content: In recent years, convolutional neural networks-based methods have been extensively applied to hyperspectral image (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) joint classification. However, most existing methods rely on fixed sliding windows for local feature extraction, making them susceptible to heterogeneous pixel interference, particularly around object boundaries and detail-rich regions. Moreover, their performance often degrades due to the limited availability of labeled samples. To address these limitations, this article proposes a joint classification network via superpixel-guided prototypical feature. Specifically, a collaborative superpixel segmentation strategy is first employed by integrating the spectral–spatial characteristics of HSI with the geometric information of LiDAR, enabling the extraction of homogeneous regions. Based on these regions, an adaptive patch restructuring strategy is introduced to generate regular-shape patches. Subsequently, these regular-shape patches are fed into a dual-branch multiscale convolutional module for hierarchical feature extraction and cross-modal fusion. Finally, class prototypes are constructed in the embedding space, and the Mahalanobis distance is adopted as the similarity metric for classification. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the propose SPFNet achieves competitive classification performance, particularly in complex scenes and few-shot scenarios.
author: Yi Yang, Shuzhen Zhang, Hailong Song, Tao Yan

title: Seeing With Words: Autocaption-Guided Graph Transformer for Remote Sensing Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing (RS) imagery is a cornerstone of geospatial analysis, which supports applications, such as land cover mapping, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. Despite significant progress with neural networks, existing approaches remain limited by their reliance on visual features alone, which often proves insufficient for distinguishing categories with similar textures or spectral signatures. In this work, we propose a novel RS segmentation framework that sees with words by integrating automatically generated image captions into a new form of graph-based reasoning. Unlike conventional graph methods that rely solely on spatial or visual similarity, we introduce a caption-aware graph construction strategy that incorporates high-level semantic cues to define patch connectivity. This novel reasoning mechanism allows the graph transformer to jointly capture spatial structure and language-guided semantics, enabling more context-aware feature aggregation. Caption features are reinjected during decoding via cross-attention to ensure that semantic guidance is preserved even when spatial similarity dominates neighbor selection. A lightweight decoder with refinement reduces patch artifacts and yields coherent high-resolution maps. Experiments on three benchmarks (LoveDA, Potsdam, and Vaihingen) show that the proposed framework achieves performance competitive with state-of-the-art methods while introducing a new language-guided paradigm for graph reasoning in RS image segmentation.
author: Ge Song, Jiawei Guo, Yang Zhang, Yu Qian, Yi Wang

title: From Measured to Experienced Heat: A Multimodal Analysis of Temperature, Urban Form, and Social Media in Mexico City
content: Urban populations face increasing exposure to high temperatures due to climate change. Yet, little is known about how residents perceive and communicate heat-related experiences and whether such expressions vary within cities. This study combines multimodal data to examine relationships between urban heat, related online discussions, socio-demographics, and urban form. We analyzed geolocated Twitter posts from Mexico City during 2022, alongside weather station air temperature, satellite-derived land surface temperature (LST), urban form represented by the local climate zones (LCZ) classification, and census indicators. The volume of heat-related tweets rises exponentially once air temperature exceeds 25 °C. In addition, LCZ characterized by higher LST exhibit a greater share of heat-related tweets. Furthermore, LCZ differ significantly in population density, age structure, internet access, and marginalization, indicating that heat-related social media activity reflects socio-thermal contrasts rather than thermal exposure alone. Thematic LLM-assisted analysis of the tweets shows that social media serves as a platform to communicate the challenges faced during periods of high temperatures, including “Health issues/Heat stress,” “Working conditions/clothes,” “Cooling/Air conditioning,” and “Harassment”. These findings show that social media can be used to assess public perceptions and lived challenges associated with urban heat and the built environment. Such insights can inform the design of human-centered climate adaptation strategies in urban settings.
author: Richard Lemoine-Rodríguez, Henri Debray, Carolin Biewer, Luis Inostroza, Hannes Taubenböck

title: A Lightweight Multimodal Spatiotemporal Learning Framework for Precipitation Nowcasting
content: Accurate and timely precipitation nowcasting is essential for meteorological hazard mitigation, particularly at monitored sites with limited sensing inputs. Capturing the nonlinear, regime-dependent relationship between precipitable water vapor (PWV) and rainfall remains challenging. This study proposes a lightweight multimodal spatiotemporal learning framework with physics-aware inductive biases for station-centered, short-horizon nowcasting within an existing or deployable monitoring network. The framework combines global navigation satellite system-derived PWV with environmental-condition variables to generate probabilistic forecasts of threshold-based precipitation events. Its architecture integrates a spatially aware multimodal module, an efficient fusion stage, and a receptance weighted key-value-based temporal dynamical module to capture spatial correlation, multimodal complementarity, and long-history temporal dependencies under practical computational constraints. Evaluation involved more than 100 stations across three climatically distinct Chinese provinces: Zhejiang, Hubei, and Sichuan. Experiments focused on 1-hour nowcasting, with extensions to 3-hour forecasts. Ablation studies confirmed the contributions of multimodal integration, long-temporal modeling, and spatial correlation modeling. Compared with the iTransformer baseline under matched evaluation conditions, the framework consistently achieved better discrimination and lower false positive rates. Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values exceeded 91% in the best-performing settings, while the false positive rate for heavy-rain events was approximately 21% at a true positive rate near 87%. Strong first-hour-of-rain accuracy further supports its potential for early warning. These results demonstrate an efficient approach to station-centered precipitation nowcasting from sparse observations.
author: Nan Zhi, Zhuwang Lv, Feng Xu, Shaojun Feng

title: Lyapunov-Guided TD3 for Secure Hyperspectral Image Transmission in STAR-RIS-Assisted Wireless Networks
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) transmission over wireless networks is constrained by the large data volume of spectral cubes, stringent delay requirements, and the risk of information leakage caused by passive eavesdropping. These challenges become more pronounced when the eavesdropper channel state information (CSI) is imperfect and communication resources must be dynamically allocated. This article presents a secure STAR-RIS-assisted HSI transmission framework that jointly considers adaptive HSI payload control, queue evolution, transmission latency, energy consumption, and secrecy outage under imperfect cascaded eavesdropper CSI. The resulting resource allocation problem is formulated as a long-term stochastic optimization problem involving active beamforming, artificial-noise transmission, STAR-RIS transmission/reflection coefficients, and adaptive HSI payload ratios. To efficiently handle the coupled optimization variables and time-varying network dynamics, a Lyapunov-guided twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (LG-TD3) algorithm is developed, where Lyapunov optimization converts the long-term objective into queue-aware per-slot optimization, while TD3 learns an effective continuous control policy. A sample-based secrecy outage evaluation mechanism is further incorporated to provide robust secure transmission without requiring perfect knowledge of the eavesdropper channels. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach converges faster than representative benchmark schemes while achieving higher secure HSI throughput, lower secrecy outage probability, reduced delivery latency, improved energy efficiency, and more effective adaptive payload control. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an efficient and robust solution for secure HSI transmission in dynamic STAR-RIS-assisted wireless environments.
author: Syed Muhammad Waqas, Fenghua Huang, Fakhar Abbas, Maazen Alsabaan, Saru Kumari, Xingsi Xue

title: Research on the Retrieval Method of 2-D Ocean Wave Spectra From Spaceborne SAR Based on Physical Feature Modulated U-Net
content: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR), owing to its high resolution, wide coverage, and all-weather, all-time observation capabilities, has become a core instrument for the dynamic monitoring of 2-D ocean wave spectra on a global scale, holding significant strategic importance for ocean dynamic research and navigation safety. However, due to the azimuth cutoff phenomenon caused by the velocity bunching effect, extracting complete ocean wave spectra from SAR image spectra is extremely difficult. To address the challenges posed by this nonlinear imaging mechanism, this article proposes a deep learning model modulated by physical features, named Wave-PMUNet. With U-Net as the backbone architecture, this model innovatively introduces the featurewise linear modulation mechanism to integrate key physical parameters, such as the azimuth cutoff wavelength, radar incidence angle, and normalized radar cross section, into the neural network. In this study, a dataset is constructed using 10 289 spatiotemporally collocated pairs of Sentinel-1 Wave Mode (WV) cross spectra and the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts fifth-generation reanalysis wave spectra. Experimental results demonstrate that without the need for a first-guess spectrum, the Wave-PMUNet model improves the retrieval accuracy and similarity index of the omnidirectional ocean wave spectra compared to the traditional generative adversarial network, as well as mainstream baseline and other representative deep learning models. Specifically, the spectral similarity index ($\Omega$) reaches 0.29, and the root-mean-square error is 0.208 m for significant wave height, 0.618 s for mean wave period, 1.597 s for peak wave period, and is reduced to 31.299$^{\circ }$ for peak wave direction, indicating competitive overall performance in ocean wave spectra retrieval. This study not only demonstrates the potential of the Wave-PMUNet model in wave spectra retrieval but also indicates that the introduction of auxiliary physical features can enhance the neural network's ability to understand the complex SAR-wave imaging mechanism. It provides a potential technical reference for spaceborne SAR ocean wave spectrum retrieval, which may contribute to improving the accuracy of global marine meteorological forecasting.
author: Yong Wan, Jiahua Jia, Weizeng Shao, Rui Zhang

title: A Spatiotemporal Fusion Method for Inland Water Quality Retrieval Products With Reduced Dependence on Coarse-Fine Image Pairing
content: Reconstructing high spatiotemporal resolution water quality products is fundamentally constrained by the tradeoffs between satellite spatial and temporal resolutions. To address this limitation, we propose the spatial and temporal linear prediction and coarse-resolution constraint fusion method (STLCCFM). This product-level fusion framework constructs a fine-resolution temporal prediction from available Landsat retrievals and subsequently constrains the overall magnitude using target-date moderate-resolution imaging spectroradiometer retrievals, with Gaussian residual redistribution applied. Unlike conventional spatiotemporal fusion (STF) methods, STLCCFM decouples temporal reconstruction from the need for strictly paired coarse-fine reference images, enabling the use of temporally sparse or spatially incomplete inputs. Validation using water transparency (Secchi disk depth, ZSD) products in Honghu Lake and Poyang Lake showed that STLCCFM achieved stronger agreement with the target-date Landsat-derived references than the compared benchmark methods. Additional experiments, including extended temporal intervals, single-sided fine-resolution inputs, and controlled geometric missing scenarios, were conducted to examine the contributions of individual components and the sensitivity of the framework to reduced fine-resolution data availability. The Taihu Lake chlorophyll-a experiment provided preliminary evidence that STLCCFM can be extended beyond ZSD retrievals. Although the fusion performance remains dependent on the quality and consistency of the input retrievals, STLCCFM provides a flexible framework for reconstructing asynchronously acquired satellite water-quality products at high spatiotemporal resolution.
author: Jiahuan Luo, Fei Xiao, Miaomiao Chen, Yi Yan, Shuhui Cao, Zhou Wang, Zhengzheng Hu, Qi Feng, Yun Du

title: SemReNet: Semantic Relational Supervision for Domain Generalization in Hyperspectral Image Classification
content: Remote sensing domain generalization aims to generalize hyperspectral image classifiers to unseen domains affected by sensor, imaging, and environmental shifts. Existing semantic-guided methods mainly rely on class-to-anchor alignment, independently matching each category to a textual anchor, which may depend on manually crafted descriptions and overlook interclass structure. We propose SemReNet, a semantic relation-preserving framework that replaces independent anchor alignment with class-level semantic relational supervision. SemReNet comprises a relational semantic encoder that constructs interclass semantic geometry and a relation-aware visual encoder that learns structured hyperspectral representations. A relational-semantic consistency objective regularizes the visual relation structure toward the semantic one during source-domain training, without enforcing absolute visual–text matching. Experiments on the Houston, Pavia, and HyRANK benchmarks show that SemReNet achieves overall accuracies of 84.21%, 88.78%, and 84.87%, outperforming the best competing methods by 1.88, 2.02, and 2.28 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of semantic relational supervision for cross-domain hyperspectral classification.
author: Qinghao Li, Binge Cui, Guangbo Ren, Haojie Li, Jianzhi Yu

title: Weakly Supervised Fine-Resolution Wildfire Fuel Mapping From Spatially Coarse Labels and Multisource Remote Sensing Data
content: Accurate large-scale wildfire fuel mapping is essential for fire-risk assessment and ecosystem management, yet fine-resolution training labels remain costly and scarce. This study presents L2HFuelNet, a weakly supervised resolution-enhancement framework that uses spatially inexact 30 m labels to generate 10 m vegetation-based fuel-type predictions in seven aggregated categories. Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery, Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar backscatter, and topographic variables are integrated through a dual-encoder architecture combining a Swin Transformer with an Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling-based convolutional encoder. A composite low-to-high loss comprising weighted cross-entropy, intersection-over-union, and confidence–vague distance terms is employed to address class imbalance and supervisory ambiguity caused by the resolution mismatch. Province-wide evaluation across the heterogeneous landscapes of Alberta, Canada, yielded an overall accuracy of 0.91 and a mean intersection-over-union of 0.84, outperforming the evaluated baselines and improving discrimination among spectrally similar classes, including Mixedwood, Pine, and Aspen. Coarse-supervision analysis further characterized class-specific label–prediction discrepancies and their influence on mapping performance. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of province-scale fine-resolution fuel characterization using coarse supervisory labels and multisource remote sensing data. The resulting categories are designed to support landscape-scale fuel assessment and can complement detailed fire behavior prediction (FBP) information when subclass-specific fire-behavior parameters are required.
author: Ehsan Khankeshizadeh, Ali Mohammadzadeh, Mohammad Marjani, Masoud Mahdianpari, Sahand Tahermanesh, Sadegh Jamali

title: Change-Aware Remote Sensing Spatiotemporal Fusion via Frequency Decoupling and Symmetric Gating
content: Remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion (STF) remains a formidable challenge in scenarios with complex land-cover changes. Existing methods generally use masking mechanisms to cover changed regions, aiming to mitigate alignment biases induced by change information. However, such indiscriminate masking strategies ignore transferable structural cues embedded in pseudo changes, leading to texture collapse and boundary degradation. To address these issues, we propose a change-aware (CA) remote sensing STF method via frequency decoupling and symmetric gating, termed CA-STF. Specifically, a wavelet feature modulation module is first designed to perform frequency decoupling, which extracts reusable structural cues from pseudo changes under low-frequency guidance while suppressing spectral perturbations. Subsequently, a spatiotemporal synergistic enhancement module employs a symmetric gating mechanism to selectively fuse the cue-enhanced features, adaptively decoupling changed and unchanged regions. Finally, a mixture-of-experts-based spatial restoration module decodes the gated features to reconstruct fine-grained textures in changed areas. Experimental results on the public the Lower Gwydir Catchment and Coleambally irrigation area datasets demonstrate that our CA-STF achieves superior fusion accuracy and visual quality in complex spatiotemporal dynamics.
author: Meng Li, Huihui Song, Xu Zhang, Kaihua Zhang

title: Dynamic Self-Attention Guidance for Layout-Consistent and Diverse Remote Sensing Image Generation
content: Text-guided remote sensing image (RSI) generation often struggles to generate layouts that strictly conform to text prompts. While existing layout-guided methods introduce additional images, such as geometric boundary maps (GBM) or real images, as reference layouts, their suboptimal layout constraint mechanisms frequently interfere with the semantic guidance of the text prompts. To address this, we propose a novel RSI generation framework that incorporates a dynamic self-attention guidance strategy. Motivated by the insight that self-attention maps inherently capture the spatial relationships between visual units during the generation process, we leverage the self-attention maps extracted from the reconstruction process of a real image as robust layout constraints. Unlike existing methods that apply constraints throughout the entire generation process, often disturbing the semantic guidance of the text prompt, we introduce a dynamic guiding strategy. This strategy injects these self-attention maps only during critical intermediate generation steps, which effectively decouples the layout guidance of the self-attention maps from the semantic guidance of the text prompt. Our method ensures that the layout of the newly generated image is constrained by the real image, while the semantic content is freely determined by the text prompt through sufficient semantic interaction. Experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms baselines in terms of layout consistency and text-guided scene diversity, and effectively improves the performance of downstream tasks, such as scene classification.
